policy.purpose: Record real defects or architecture failures that must not recur.
policy.rule: Every entry names the canonical regression proof. This corpus is not a bug tracker or quality score.

cases.failure: animation-native-intelligence imported retired ./animation-runtime-wiring and broke source closure/docs generation.
cases.invariant: Retired wiring modules are absent and canonical runtime contract owners are present.

cases.failure: Ambiguous/malformed Host or Origin framing could reach application handling inconsistently.
cases.invariant: Malformed or ambiguous HTTP framing fails closed before MCP dispatch.

cases.failure: Export replacement could follow a symbolic-link destination and create-new used a check-then-write race.
cases.invariant: Exports reject symbolic-link/non-file destinations and new files use exclusive create semantics.

cases.failure: A single SDK v2 handler emitted SSE for legacy 2025 traffic despite the required JSON compatibility contract.
cases.invariant: Modern 2026 traffic uses createMcpHandler while legacy 2025 compatibility remains request-owned JSON through the bounded SDK shim.

cases.failure: Gateway auto negotiation could fall back without exposing which MCP protocol era was actually connected.
cases.invariant: Connected protocol era is retained for status diagnostics and cleared on disconnect.

cases.failure: RuntimeHost stored profile/phase shadow state even though request handling used the canonical Runtime registry.
cases.invariant: RuntimeHost owns listener lifecycle only; profile/phase ownership remains in the Runtime registry.

cases.failure: REFERENCE.json and workspace README.md could be read without a size bound.
cases.invariant: Control context documents are bounded before full reads and oversized files fail closed.

cases.failure: LazyDesigner technical product identity still pointed to the prior BuildIT repository after the product rename.
cases.invariant: Technical repository identity points to the LazyDesigner source authority while human-facing plugin metadata remains anonymous.
